name: The Circuit
description:
The Circuit started as a server farm. Specifically, it started as twelve city
blocks of data centers that Axiom Industries decommissioned when they moved to
quantum infrastructure and couldn't be bothered to demolish. Within six months,
the hollowed-out server racks had been converted into market stalls, the cooling
systems had been repurposed for climate control, and the backup generators were
running what might be the most productive illegal economy in the western
hemisphere. The Circuit is Meridian's black market, tech bazaar, and unofficial
innovation hub. It's where you go to buy augments that aren't in the corporate
catalog, sell data you shouldn't have, or hire someone whose skillset doesn't
appear on any licensed professional registry.

The aesthetic is neo-noir flea market — tangled cables overhead like vines in a
digital jungle, holographic price tags floating above stalls selling everything
from military-grade neural interfaces to homemade ramen. Rogue AIs run some of
the shops, their consciousness distributed across salvaged hardware, negotiating
prices through speakers bolted to the walls. Data brokers sit in neon-lit alcoves,
trading corporate secrets like baseball cards. Augment shops range from genuinely
skilled technicians doing unlicensed but excellent work to butchers who'll install
anything in anyone for the right price. The Circuit has its own internal economy,
its own reputation systems, and its own justice — which mostly amounts to "cheat
someone and see what happens."

This is Robin Hood territory. The Collective operates openly here, redistributing
stolen corporate data, running free net access points, and maintaining the
Circuit's infrastructure as a public service. The philosophy is simple: the corps
stole everything first, so stealing it back is just accounting. Not everyone in
the Circuit is an idealist — plenty of people here are straightforward criminals
who'd sell their grandmother's augments for the right price — but the idealism
provides a framework, a story the Circuit tells about itself. And stories matter,
especially in a city that runs on corporate ones.

sights: Cables and fiber optics strung overhead in dense canopies, pulsing with data traffic
Holographic signage in every color, advertising in Shelf Cant, Standard, and machine code
Stalls built into decommissioned server racks — some still have the original Axiom branding
Rogue AIs manifesting as floating geometric shapes, holographic animals, or just text on a wall
Augment technicians working in open-air shops, chrome and flesh under bright surgical lights
Data brokers in neon-lit alcoves, faces hidden behind privacy screens
The occasional spark shower from someone doing something ambitious with a soldering iron
Screens everywhere — showing net traffic visualizations, security feeds, pirated entertainment, and art
sounds: The hum of repurposed cooling systems — a low, constant thrum that the Circuit is built on
Haggling in five languages plus machine code
Electronic music from competing stalls, creating an accidental remix that changes block to block
The whine of augment calibration tools
AI voices — some human-passing, some deliberately synthetic, some that sound like singing math
The occasional shout of 'SWEEP' when someone spots an Axiom Security drone, followed by coordinated scrambling
smells: Ozone and hot solder — the smell of tech being born
Street food — the Circuit has the best dumplings in Meridian, and this is not debatable
Coolant fluid leaking from overtaxed server repurposements
The sharp, clean smell of brand-new augment components, fresh from the smuggling crate
Energy drinks. So many energy drinks. The Circuit runs on caffeine and bad decisions.
atmosphere.feel:
Electric. The Circuit buzzes with possibility and danger in equal measure. It
feels like the internet made physical — chaotic, creative, democratic in theory,
predatory in practice, and absolutely vital. There's an energy here that the Core
can't replicate with all its optimization: the energy of people building things
because they want to, not because a quarterly target demands it. It's exciting.
It's also the kind of place where you check your wallet, your augments, and your
exits, in that order.

demographics: A dense, hyper-diverse population of roughly 200,000, skewing young, technically literate, and economically informal. Heavy representation of first-generation immigrants, former corpo contract workers who aged out of usefulness, and self-taught engineers. Tier 1 and Tier 2 predominate, with a small but influential class of unlicensed entrepreneurs who would be Tier 3 if anyone were issuing paperwork. The Circuit does not ask where you came from.
dangers: Scams — the Circuit's reputation system is imperfect and exploitable
Bad augment work — unlicensed doesn't always mean skilled
Data theft — your personal information is a commodity here
Axiom Security sweeps — rare but devastating when they happen
Rogue AI instability — most are fine, some are very much not fine
Getting in over your head — the Circuit will sell you anything, including trouble
Addiction — the Circuit has stimulants, neural narcotics, and experience chips that are hard to put down
Owing the wrong people — debts in the Circuit are collected creatively
opportunities: Cutting-edge augment technology, available nowhere else
Data — corporate secrets, personal information, historical records the corps tried to delete
Contracts — the Circuit is where fixers find operators for every kind of job
Community — the Circuit's maker culture is genuine and generative
Free net access — Collective-maintained nodes, uncensored and unmonitored
AI collaboration — working with rogue AIs who think differently than any human
story_hooks: The rogue AI who runs the Circuit's most reliable augment shop — and who might know something about Kyle's past
The Collective's open-source weapon designs — making arms impossible to monopolize
A data cache from the Corporate Wars surfaces in the Circuit, containing something someone will kill to suppress
The Circuit's annual 'Swap Meet' — a massive bazaar where anything goes, and frequently does
Kyle's fixer — the person who finds him work — operates out of a Circuit noodle shop
The tension between the Circuit's idealism and its reality — Robin Hood mythology vs. actual crime

adjacent_to: the Gray Zone (connected by the Underpass — a converted drainage tunnel)
The Meridian Core (hard border — security checkpoint, heavily monitored)

frequented_by: Hackers, data brokers, and information merchants
Rogue AIs operating businesses or just existing freely
Fixers who broker contracts between clients and operators like Kyle
Corporate employees shopping for things their employer won't provide
Artists, musicians, and creators who can't afford Core gallery fees
People who need to disappear and the people who help them do it
